solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Choose not to take part in work with solicitor

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a tout solicits custom, pestering people to buy

explanation.surface: Someone declines to join a job alongside their lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like the British word for a lawyer, but here it is literally one who solicits: a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb describes formally withdrawing from a scheme or activity, declining to participate.

clue.text: In part, Republican denies manoeuvring for the top job?

definitions.note: the answer is the person holding the top job, signalled by the question mark

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving things about tactically, so these letters are rearranged
being in something means sitting inside it, so the following letters are placed within the outer pair

blocks.note: PT is the standard abbreviation for part
R abbreviates Republican
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Republican politician plays down jockeying for the White House.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'In part' as 'partly', but it is an instruction to put letters inside PT, the abbreviation for part.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is whoever holds the highest office of a republic or organisation, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Old writer featuring in upcoming total collected works

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from bottom to top, so the word is turned around
to feature in something is to appear within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: O is the usual abbreviation for old
a nib is the writing point of a pen
a sum is a total

explanation.surface: An ancient author appears in a forthcoming complete edition of their output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old writer' looks like one ancient author, but it splits into two pieces: the abbreviation for old and a pen's nib.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus edition gathers several works by one author into a single volume.

clue.text: Cup match level until just before the end

indicators.note: stopping just short of the end means the final letter is not reached

blocks.note: scores that are level are all square, finishing equal

explanation.surface: A cup game stays all square until the dying moments.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football a cup tie is a knockout match; the surface hints at a draw, which is a different sense of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: British usage calls a knockout game in a cup competition a tie, as in a third-round tie.

clue.text: Fine food shop to provide food, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a deli, or delicatessen, sells prepared foods
to cater is to supply food for an event

explanation.surface: A posh food shop mostly provides catering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine food shop' reads as one phrase, but 'Fine' is the definition and 'food shop' alone is the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine and delicate are synonyms describing something thin, light and easily damaged, like fine lace.

clue.text: Greek party in charge of suppressing resistance

indicators.note: suppressing something means holding it down inside, so one piece is kept within the others

blocks.note: a do is a party
R is the physics symbol for resistance
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A Greek political party in power crushes the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek party' looks like one political group, but 'Greek' is the definition and 'party' is a social do.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is an ancient Greek dialect and architectural order, so the adjective means of a Greek people.

clue.text: Support key objective with sources of extra reserved money

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letters are taken

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or a body
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
an end is an aim or objective
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Backing a key aim with spare cash set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support key objective' reads as a phrase about strategy, but it is three separate pieces: a leg, a keyboard key and an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is currency that must be accepted by law in payment of a debt.

clue.text: Nicola messily devours the filling from any creamy pastry

indicators.note: doing something messily leaves things in disorder, so the letters are jumbled
a filling sits in the middle, so only the central letter is taken
to devour is to swallow, so one piece ends up inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the middle letter of this word

explanation.surface: Nicola eats a cream-filled pastry, spilling the filling everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is anagram fodder whose letters are already almost the answer; the middle letter of 'any' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannoli are Sicilian tubes of fried pastry stuffed with sweet ricotta cream.

clue.text: Cycle around centre of big Italian city

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps another
the centre of a word is its middle, so only the central letter is taken

blocks.note: a turn is one cycle or rotation
the middle letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone bikes around the middle of a large Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' suggests riding a bicycle, but here it is a noun meaning one rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin, or Torino, is the capital of Piedmont in northern Italy, home of Fiat and Juventus.

clue.text: Check next to one river and another for animals

blocks.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
another river, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: An inspection beside two rivers to look for wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One river' is a named river, and 'another' is a second river given only by its abbreviation R.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer are Arctic deer, a plural noun matching the plural animals.

clue.text: Elite individuals go after information

indicators.note: coming after something means following it, so the piece named first is placed second

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: Top people pursue information.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece comes 'after' the first, so the clue's order is reversed in the answer. Gen is British slang for the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the upper-class landowning people just below the nobility, a social elite.

clue.text: Terribly bad, bad local I repeatedly trashed

indicators.note: something trashed has been wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: both words taken as written, the adjective here being a second use after the one in the definition
the letter I used twice

explanation.surface: A dreadful pub got wrecked, and the speaker keeps trashing it.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a British word for one's nearby pub. 'Repeatedly' tells you to use the I twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolical, literally devilish, is common informal British for appallingly poor in quality.

clue.text: Political group identified by your and my piece in LA Times

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so these letters go within the outer pair

blocks.note: taken as written
what belongs to you and me is ours
a part is a piece
in measurements, times is by, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A party is profiled in an article in the Los Angeles Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'LA Times' looks like the newspaper, but 'Times' is the multiplication sign read as 'by'. Labour is one of Britain's two main parties.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour Party is the main centre-left party in British politics, a political organisation.

clue.text: Has drinks, but no starter

indicators.note: with no starter, the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: to down a drink is to swallow it quickly

explanation.surface: Someone takes drinks but skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' suggests the first course of a meal, but here it is the first letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something is to possess it, and to own is to possess as property.

clue.text: Article in Libération covering Northern French city

indicators.note: a covering goes round what it covers, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: les is the plural definite article in French
N abbreviates Northern

explanation.surface: A piece in the Paris newspaper Libération about a city in northern France.
explanation.walkthrough: Libération is a French newspaper, so an 'article' in it looks like a news story, but it is a grammatical article in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Lens is a former coal-mining town in the Pas-de-Calais region of northern France.

clue.text: Beset by trouble, degenerate shows sign of slowing down

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a blight is a cause of trouble or ruin
a rake is a dissolute man

explanation.surface: A troubled reprobate shows signs of slowing down in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degenerate' reads as an adjective or verb, but it is a noun for a debauched person.
explanation.definitionFit: The red lamp on a vehicle's rear comes on when the driver presses the pedal to reduce speed.

clue.text: Fit cheap, tatty clothes

indicators.note: as a verb, to clothe is to cover, so the letters are dressed inside the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Cheap, scruffy garments that fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as a noun for garments, but it is a verb: the words dress the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt and fit are synonyms meaning suitable or appropriate for the purpose.

clue.text: Cold male lacking pretence

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
artless means natural and without guile

explanation.surface: A frosty man who never pretends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold male' reads as a description of one man, but the definition is just 'Cold'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold person is unfeeling and lacks compassion, which is what heartless means.

clue.text: Frequent drinking you ultimately had reduced

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so one piece swallows the other
ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is taken

blocks.note: to frequent a place is to attend it regularly
the last letter of this word
to have a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: A regular drinker finds the drinking eventually cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frequent' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to visit often. 'Had' is in the sense of having dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Attenuated describes something weakened, thinned or lessened in force or amount.

clue.text: I shout out loud and look up and down

indicators.note: saying something out loud means only its sound counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: the pronoun and the organ of sight sound alike
to bawl is to shout, and it sounds like a ball

explanation.surface: Someone yells and then stares at a person from head to toe.
explanation.walkthrough: The pronoun becomes the organ of sight, and a word for shouting becomes a round toy.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them closely, often looking them over from head to foot.

clue.text: Prejudice in book reported to be cut back

indicators.note: cutting something shortens it, so the final letter is dropped
going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
what is reported is said

explanation.surface: Bigotry in a book is said to have been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' sounds like a homophone signal, but here it is simply a synonym for spoken words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is an unfair inclination for or against someone, the same as a preconceived prejudice.

clue.text: Somebody maybe taking a punt eating tail of foul fish

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within the other
a tail is the hind end, so only the last letter is taken

blocks.note: a person out in a punt, a flat river boat, is a boater
the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A gambler eats the tail end of a nasty-smelling fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking a punt' suggests placing a bet, but a punt is also a flat-bottomed boat poled along a river, as in Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloater is a whole herring that is salted and lightly smoked, a type of fish.

clue.text: Tool does some calculations, we’re told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: someone who does sums adds

explanation.surface: A tool that does arithmetic, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first word; the rest is a verb phrase for doing sums, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is an axe-like woodworking implement with its blade set at right angles to the handle.

clue.text: Excellent, regularly noted author

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter, so alternate ones are kept

blocks.note: def is slang for excellent
the second and fourth letters of this word

explanation.surface: Praise for a writer who is consistently acclaimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted author' reads as one phrase, but 'noted' is the source of letters and 'author' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English writer of Robinson Crusoe and Moll Flanders.

clue.text: Vessels requiring knotted ropes at bow

indicators.note: knotted things are twisted and tangled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ships that need ropes tied at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word after the link is fodder, including the nautical 'bow', which fits the surface so well it seems to be setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Powerboats are fast motor-driven craft, and boats of any kind are vessels.

clue.text: Overcome, journalist enjoyed the delights of Bordeaux?

blocks.note: to win is to overcome opposition
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist, overwhelmed, indulged in fine claret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overcome' looks like a past participle describing the journalist, but it is a verb in the base form.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is the French wine region, so enjoying its delights means drinking its wine; the question mark flags the indirect hint.

clue.text: A very loud, cool thing

blocks.note: taken as written
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
to air a room is to let it cool

explanation.surface: A thing that is very loud yet cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' looks like an adjective of approval, but it is a verb, as in airing a room.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can mean any matter or event, as in a grand affair, so it is a general word for a thing.

clue.text: It’s not important to gossip about an award

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: to natter is to chat idly
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Chattering about a prize is unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour awarded by the monarch, abbreviated OM.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to dismiss something as insignificant, meaning it makes no difference.

clue.text: One held by host?

indicators.note: something held is gripped inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event

explanation.surface: Something a presenter holds.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: a presenter grips a microphone, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere or quizmaster typically speaks into a handheld microphone, the thing carried by the host.

clue.text: Used sneaky tactic filling in legal document

indicators.note: filling something in means occupying its inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a deed is a signed legal document
a ploy is a cunning manoeuvre

explanation.surface: Someone used underhand tricks to complete a legal form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling in' suggests completing a form, but it is the instruction to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To deploy resources is to bring them into effective action, so deployed means put to use.

clue.text: Short, extremely showy gesture of respect

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: curt means brief or abrupt
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A brief, flamboyant bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely showy' reads as 'very showy', but it means the extreme letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsy is a bob made by bending the knees, traditionally performed by women to show deference.
